newsitem.title: GERMANY: Oil World details 96/97, 97/98 oilseeds estimates.
newsitem.headline: Oil World details 96/97, 97/98 oilseeds estimates.

text.p: The independent Oil World newsletter has cut is forecasts for global output of 10 key oilseeds in both the 1996/97 and 1997/98 seasons.
Production in the current season was pegged at 256.5 million tonnes, virtually unchanged from 256.2 million in 95/96 but below an April 11 estimate for 96/97 of 257.3 million.
Oil World said Brazil and Argentina were now expecting to harvest fewer soybeans although this was partly offset by India, which had raised its crop forecasts.

With oilseeds consumption advancing rapidly, end-season stocks were forecast at 25.5 million tonnes, down from 27.2 million projected for the end of 96/97 a month ago and compared with 31.7 million tonnes at the end of the 95/96 season.
Output of oilseeds in 97/98 was forecast at 274.3 million tonnes, 17.8 million above 96/97.
Oil World a month ago expected a 19.1 million tonnes increase over 96/97 in the new season.
It cited expectations of lower Canadian and Chinese rapeseed crops, among other factors.
World oilseeds stocks at the end of 97/98 were tentatively pegged at 27 million tonnes.
